Welcome to the Merrikhi Lab

Understanding how cognitive processes interact with the neural mechanisms underlying speech perception and production, with the goal of improving the assessment and treatment of communication disorders.

Explore our researchJoin the lab
Department of Communication Sciences and DisordersArnold School of Public Health | University of South Carolina

Speaking requires the rapid coordination of memory, attention, hearing, and movement. We study how these cognitive and sensorimotor processes are implemented within the neural systems that support speech perception and production.

Our research focuses particularly on how working memory and attention interact with the neural systems involved in speech. We examine these processes in healthy individuals and clinical populations with communication disorders across the lifespan.

By combining behavioral research with neurophysiological methods, brain stimulation, computational approaches, and artificial intelligence, we examine how speech is planned, monitored, controlled, and learned. We use these complementary approaches to identify mechanisms that may inform more effective and personalized approaches to communication disorders.

Our goal

To connect fundamental discoveries about the cognitive and neural mechanisms underlying speech with new ways to understand individual differences and improve communication outcomes.

Our Research

Our research examines the neural systems that allow people to perceive, plan, produce, monitor, and learn speech. We study how working memory, attention, sensory processing, and motor control contribute to these functions across the lifespan in healthy individuals and people with communication disorders.

Cognition & Speech

Speech perception and production depend on cognitive processes that help us maintain, select, and use information. We investigate how working memory, attention, and related cognitive processes interact with the neural mechanisms underlying speech.

Neural Mechanisms of Speech Motor Control

We study the neural mechanisms of speech motor control, including the processes that support speech planning, production, monitoring, and learning. This work examines how neural systems integrate sensory information to produce speech that is accurate, flexible, and responsive to changing demands.

Communication Disorders & AI

We investigate how speech and cognitive mechanisms may differ in people with communication disorders. We also use computational and artificial intelligence approaches to uncover patterns in behavioral and neural data and to help inform more effective and personalized assessment and intervention.

People

Yaser Merrikhi, Ph.D.

Director, Speech and Cognition Research Laboratory
Assistant Professor, Department of Communication Sciences and Disorders
Arnold School of Public Health, University of South Carolina

Dr. Merrikhi's interdisciplinary research integrates cognitive neuroscience, speech science, and biomedical engineering. His work uses behavioral, neurophysiological, brain stimulation, computational, and artificial intelligence approaches to study human speech and communication.
